html:
SMTO-AUT-0001 — SMTO needs a username or password to continue

GUID: eb13f1ff-6e53-4e37-8f2d-64be05529f00
Slug: credential-required
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: aut

What happened

  • The connection this Task is using is missing sign-in details, such as a username or password, so SMTO stopped before connecting. Nothing ran on that connection, and this doesn't mean a password you gave was wrong.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If SMTO asks you in the conversation for a username or password, type the requested details in your reply to that question. SMTO waits for these details and then tries the same connection again with them.
  2. To avoid being asked every time, open Parameter Store, find the saved entry for this connection, and fill in its username and password. When a saved connection already has its sign-in details, SMTO can connect without stopping to ask.
  3. Don't type passwords into your original Task request, into a command, or into screenshots. Text in those places can show up in the Task history and logs, where others might see it.

What success looks like

  • The step that stopped continues and shows its result instead of credential required.

If it still fails

  • If SMTO keeps asking even after you give the details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't include the password itself in that message.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A connection skill (database, HTTP or Proxmox) or the managed sudo path stopped before dispatch because required authentication fields were empty or sudo reported that a password is required.

What this means

  • Required authentication fields are absent, or sudo output indicates that interactive credentials are needed; this does not establish that supplied credentials were wrong. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • Required authentication fields are absent, or sudo output indicates that interactive credentials are needed; this does not establish that supplied credentials were wrong.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect missing_fields or the elevation authentication stage; distinguish missing values from provider rejection.

How to fix it

  • Check missing_fields and parameter_key in the result: fill user/password (or the HTTP profile's auth fields) in that Parameter Store record, or let the Agent collect them through ask_user as transient auth_values or sudo_password. Never embed secrets in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostics.
  • Provide the required fields through the supported credential or Parameter Store flow. Never embed secrets in task instructions or shell commands.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected flow has its required private fields and proceeds through its normal authentication check.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
